website: Jay's Apparel - static e-commerce site for sustainable clothing
original_issues: Basic Tailwind-styled HTML with hardcoded colors (#db2777/pink-600, #fbcfe8/pink-300), generic product cards, minimal interactivity
improvements_made: Complete design token system (CSS variables: --brand-primary #db2777, --gray-50 through --gray-900, semantic colors)

Apple Design principles applied: response/latency (:active feedback), interruptibility (from current value), springs (critically damped default), materials (backdrop-filter), reduced motion, optical sizing typography
UI/UX consistency: identical nav, mobile menu, footer across all 3 pages
60-30-10 color rule implementation: 60% neutral gray, 30% brand pink, 10% accent
Accessibility: focus-visible on all interactive elements, prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-reduced-transparency media queries
Responsive design: mobile-first grid (1→3 columns), fixed header with 5rem padding, max-width 1280px
Optical sizing: negative tracking on display text (-0.02em), comfortable leading on body (1.6)
audience: General consumers interested in sustainable fashion; non-technical solopreneurs as user context
technology: Static HTML5 + Tailwind CSS via CDN + vanilla JavaScript, no build step required
key_decisions: Applied Apple Design principles to a static e-commerce site
Mixed ui-ux-pro-max-plus principles with apple-design principles
Used CSS custom properties for theming consistency
Added accessibility media queries as core, not afterthought
